Subject: Co-sell eligibility and offer fractionation — cloud marketplace decisions

Hi Jamie / Aline —

Thanks for taking this on. Attached is an initial eligibility matrix and a simple sketch of offer surface we think maps best to co-sell triggers for enterprise leads (see attachments: eligibility_matrix_v1.xlsx, pack_surface_sketch.png). High level proposal below so we can align on what each marketplace needs from a listing and co-sell perspective.

Key proposal (short):
- Offer surface: one "Core Hosted API" SKU on all three clouds (AWS/Azure/GCP) + a small set of add-on SKUs: "Reserved Dedicated (contracted)" and "Quantity Tiers".
- Fractionation: publish the Core SKU as global (multi-region) where possible; publish Dedicated/Reserved SKUs only in certified regions to control capacity & support SLAs.
- Co-sell eligibility: require 1) enterprise contact verified, and 2) customer > committed monthly spend threshold OR procurement contract in place. Co-sell flag flips on once MSP/AM verifies.
- Pricing bands: keep identical list price for Core across clouds; regional discounts applied downstream. Dedicated SKU will be a separate list price with metadata linking to reserved contract (legal).

Open questions for marketplace teams:
- How granular should region-level SKUs be to satisfy co-sell referral rules? (single global SKU vs per-region listing)
- Any manifest or contract metadata fields needed to link a listing to a Redwood Dedicated contract id?
- Lead flow: confirm how co-sell leads are routed (HubSpot lead id mapping or partner portal payload?).

Next steps we propose:
1) Jamie/Aline: confirm platform-side constraints for listing (manifest fields, regional gating)
2) Redwood: finalize eligibility_matrix_v1.xlsx and produce a small sample manifest for Core and Dedicated SKUs
3) Legal/Procurement: prepare a short template for dedicated-contract linkage (we'll loop procurement@acme.com for formatting)

Attaching: eligibility_matrix_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), pack_surface_sketch.png (diagram).

Thanks — hoping to lock this by EOD Wednesday so Marissa can include in the co-sell enablement pack.

Thanks Soojin — this is a helpful start. A few clarifying points from AWS Marketplace side: 

- Regional SKUs: AWS prefers fewer SKUs in most cases; a single global listing with region attributes is acceptable and simplifies co-sell tracking. However, if you need dedicated capacity to be constrained by region (e.g., EU-only GPUs), you should publish a region-tagged variant.
- Manifest linkage: we can accept a custom metadata field ("partner_contract_id") in the listing manifest that points to your reserved contract. That will be visible to our co-sell team and can be used for lead qualification.
- Co-sell payload: we can push leads using either a HubSpot ID or the partner portal webhook. HubSpot mapping is easiest if you can supply a sample payload.

Quick ask: can you confirm the list-price vs committed-price model for Dedicated? If the dedicated SKU requires a separate SOW, we recommend flagging it in the manifest so our reps see it at lead intake.

On timelines: once we have the manifest sample and the eligibility spreadsheet, we can open the co-sell enablement ticket. Typical lead time for full co-sell onboarding is 4–6 weeks.

Jamie O'Neill
Partner Programs — AWS Marketplace
jamie.oneill@awsmarketplace.com

Folks — thanks Jamie. Based on the AWS guidance and internal constraints I propose the following concrete mapping (we should finalize in the eligibility matrix):

- Core Hosted API (SKU: RW-HOST-CORE) — published globally on AWS/Azure/GCP, single listing with region attributes. Co-sell eligible on lead verification (AM sign-off).
- Dedicated Reserved (SKU: RW-DEDI-RES) — published as region-flagged variants only in certified regions (us-west-2, us-east-1, europe-west1 for initial rollouts). This SKU will include partner_contract_id metadata linking to the reserved contract.
- Add-on quantity tiers (SKU family: RW-ADD-*) — published per-cloud but not required for co-sell eligibility (sales enablement only).

Action items I can own:
- Update eligibility_matrix_v1.xlsx with the above mapping and include thresholds (monthly committed spend, minimum term).
- Produce sample manifest snippets for Core and Dedicated (will drop into the Drive link).
- Sync with Legal to ensure the contract ID flow works (cc Marissa for procurement).

If that sounds good I'll lock the matrix and sample manifests by EOD today. Marissa — once locked, can you confirm we should include a one-pager for field reps summarizing the co-sell triggers?

Thanks,
